The Softie sleeping bags (also called the Merlin, the Merlin 3, or the Merlin 3-season) are a range of 4 ¼ kg insulated sleeping bags, currently in 6 ft (1.80 m) (US), 5.25 ft (1.60 m), or 5 ft 6 in (1.70 m) (UK) (UK) lengths, designed and marketed by the American company The North Face. Since the North Face acquired them in 2006 from the bankrupt Mammut Outdoor, the Merlins are currently marketed as The North Face Merlins. From 2006 to 2008, the Merlins were made in Poland, but since 2008 production has been in New Zealand. The Merlins are the original nylon-filled bags and were first sold by the U.S. branch of The North Face in 1989, under the name "Premier" (which was used on their other nylon sleeping bags as well). The Merlins are popular around the world, but are most popular among trekkers, and mountaineers, and are still the most popular sleeping bags from The North Face. The Merlin 4 ¼ kg in the US is a 6 ft sleeping bag. The Merlins have also earned fame as the sleeping bag of legend mountaineers of the modern era. Some notable users include the brothers of the Mount Everest first two summiters, Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay. Other Merlins are used by professional climbers to compete in the sport of big wall free climbing. For a while while Merlins were the most popular sleeping bags used by the professional free climber's community they are now superseded by K2 bags. The Merlins have become iconic, both among free climbers and trekkers worldwide.
